speech_verification.heard: April 14, 1935, dawned with a clear blue sky. By afternoon, birds and jackrabbits fled the Oklahoma plains. A wall of 300,000 tons of topsoil struck Oklahoma. It turned so black people could not see their hands. Families hung wet sheets and rubbed Vaseline in their nostrils. Woody Guthrie watched the dust turn day into total night. They waited in darkness for a clear blue sky.
